what: When the cursor is over the photo (turns on in .3s power2.out), droplets of radius 96px dropped every 10px of travel melt together into an open window, and through it a grid paper in the background color (1px grid line color · cells of about 20px that fit the panel exactly) shows. The droplet under the cursor has .62× radius and trails the cursor by .17, so the window stays open when the cursor stops, and passed droplets fill in .22s and settle over 1.5s. The window edge ripples 44px inward with two layers of noise (105px cells · .5 speed), and the same gesture sends ripple rings across the photo at 300px per second (crest spacing 105 · width 75 · rises in .1s and decays at 1.15), bending only the photo by up to 26px. On release it switches off in .55s power2.inOut

options.base: Reference width (px) for scaling values down in proportion to screen width — at 1440, the 1440 version values are multiplied by innerWidth/1440. If absent, kept as is (px)
options.hold: Droplet size multiplier under the hand, default .62
options.every: Distance the droplet-dropping hand travels (px), default 10
options.glide: Ratio at which the drop under the Interaction point follows it (per Frame), default .17
options.ring-speed · ring-wave · ring-width · ri: Ripple ring speed (px/s), crest spacing, width, decay and rise (seconds), default 300 · 105 · 75 · 1.15 · .1
options.bend: How much the ripples bend the photo (px), default 26 — 0 means no bending
options.wobble · wobble-size · wobble-speed: Edge ripple width (px) · pitch (px) · speed, default 44 · 105 · .5
options.data-open: The element’s data-open (0 to 50, %) — crops that much from all four sides. The side that opens it with clip-path inset on entry writes the same value every frame, so the shader panel opens along with it.
options.[data-fx-part=picture]: Photo — If it is a real image, that image is used. If it is a placeholder (.wf-img data-label), the same shape is drawn and applied. When moved with GSAP (parallax), the spot inside the panel follows too

note: One canvas fixed to the screen (z-index 0, at the very front of body) carries a plate for each photo — text covering a photo needs a position so it sits above the canvas. If the image URL is on another domain, CORS must be open. With reduced motion · on touch devices it is not applied and the DOM photos are left as is. The formulas were measured from the original and rewritten

from.where: index.html .g-entry__frame (18 photos in the lecture cells) — original [data-media] OGL shader
